classification.difficultyReason: Match vertices across differently oriented triangles and select SSS, RHS, SAS or AAS from the supplied givens.

content.prompt: For each pair, write a congruence statement and give a reason.

spec.description: Two triangles side by side, retaining all six numerical labels and their vertex associations. Neither triangle has a right-angle mark. Ordinary source blue outlines are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: AB=FE=3.5 cm; AC=FD=2 cm; BC=ED=4 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied givens remain visible; no congruence statement or test is supplied.

answer.worked:
$AB=FE=3.5\text{ cm}$, $BC=ED=4\text{ cm}$ and $AC=FD=2\text{ cm}$.

Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle FED$ (SSS).

spec.description: Left triangle has its right angle at B; right triangle has its right angle at E. Both hypotenuse labels and both 3 cm leg labels are retained. Ordinary outlines and marks use black.
spec.mathematics: Angle ABC=angle DEF=90 degrees; AC=DF=5 cm; AB=DE=3 cm.

answer.worked:
$\angle ABC=\angle DEF=90^\circ$, $AC=DF=5\text{ cm}$ and $AB=DE=3\text{ cm}$.

The right angles, hypotenuses and another pair of sides are equal. Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle DEF$ (RHS).

spec.sourceRegion: Review exercise 3c, left ABC and right DEF
spec.description: One editable paired figure preserves the comparison row: ABC on the left and DEF on the right. The 100 degree labels lie inside the sectors at C and F. No angle arcs are added.
spec.mathematics: AC=EF=3 cm; BC=DF=5 cm; angle ACB=angle DFE=100 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied sides, angles and vertex names are visible.

answer.worked:
$AC=EF=3\text{ cm}$, $BC=DF=5\text{ cm}$ and $\angle ACB=\angle EFD=100^\circ$.

The equal angles are included between the corresponding equal sides. Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle EDF$ (SAS).

spec.sourceRegion: Review exercise 3d, left ABC and right DEF
spec.description: Paired figures preserve the left/right comparison, all vertex names, both 6 cm labels, and the 40 and 25 degree labels in their source sectors. Ordinary outlines and labels use black.
spec.mathematics: AC=ED=6 cm; angle BAC=angle DEF=40 degrees; angle ACB=angle EDF=25 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: No third-angle value or congruence conclusion is supplied.

answer.worked:
$\angle BAC=\angle FED=40^\circ$, $\angle ACB=\angle EDF=25^\circ$ and $AC=ED=6\text{ cm}$.

Two corresponding angles and a matching side are equal. Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle EFD$ (AAS).
